candidates.text: injectSweepAndCall must be restricted to delegatecall-only execution, e.g. via the onlyDelegatecall modifier, so it cannot execute as a direct external call on the router.
evidence_ids: Use the existing onlyDelegatecall modifier from DelegatecallGuard on injectSweepAndCall, and add a short doc comment making the assumption explicit.

candidates.text: The router must remain pure logic with no long-term funds; all balances belong to the calling wallet, so direct calls must not cause the router to accumulate and control user funds.
evidence_ids: This mismatch between intended execution context (delegatecall into a wallet/shim) and actual allowed execution context (direct external call on the router) causes the router to accumulate and control user funds. The core faulty assumption is that “this function will only ever execute in a context where address(this) is a wallet (or shim) owned by the user”; in reality, it is fully callable on the router implementation itself, turning a stateless routing component into a stateful asset custodian and significantly increasing blast radius for any other bug.
The router is effectively “pure logic” with no long-term funds; all balances belong to the calling wallet.
